Subject: Security exhibit questions — pen test notice & evidence cadence

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for sending the draft. A couple quick asks from Remedy before we can move the order form forward:

- We need clarification on the pen-test notice requirement: Remedy policy requires a 48-hour window for scheduled tests (our security team prefers 48h) and a copy of the test plan. Can Redwood support that?
- Please confirm SOC 2 availability and whether you’ll provide a current report and the scope (type II and timeframe).
- What is your proposed evidence cadence for operational artifacts (logs, patch history, sample configs)? Our procurement team expects a weekly snapshot during the onboarding month, then monthly after.

Can you confirm these items and share where you’ll host evidence (Drive, S3, portal)? We’d like to avoid a long procurement loop — if you can confirm by Friday EOD we’ll try to keep the contract on track.

Attaching a short internal checklist from Remedy for context.

Regards,
Sarah
Sarah Tan
Security Program Manager — Remedy Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions — pen test notice & evidence cadence

Hi Sarah — thanks for the checklist and the clear asks. High-level responses below; please see attached Draft_Security_Exhibit_v3.pdf for the full proposed language.

1) Pen-test notice: our standard is 7 business days for non-emergency scheduled tests with a signed statement of intent and scoping. That said, we understand Remedy's 48-hour preference. Proposed compromise: 72 hours operational notice for low-impact, agreed vendor tests, and 7 business days for broader engagement. We can include a one-time exception for a 48-hour scheduled test with pre-approved scope.

2) SOC 2: we will provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report upon execution of a mutual NDA and Order Form. The exhibit will commit to providing the annual report and SSAE mapping (if requested).

3) Evidence cadence: proposed cadence is weekly snapshots during the first 30 days of onboarding (sample sets limited to non-production artifacts), then monthly thereafter. Evidence will be provided via a secure Drive folder and expiring S3 links; we’ll include an audit log for access.

We are attaching a redline-ready order form (OrderForm_Redlines_20250709.docx) and the v3 of the security exhibit for Remedy’s review. I’m looping in Kimberly (legal) and Karthik (infosec) to confirm the proposed notice compromise and evidence controls.

If Remedy can confirm acceptance of the compromise by Friday EOD, Ben will proceed with the Order Form signature path and we’ll provide the DocuSign link.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_Security_Exhibit_v3.pdf (PDF stub), OrderForm_Redlines_20250709.docx (docx stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit language — legal redlines & suggested edits

Naomi / team — reviewed the v3 exhibit and the proposed notice compromise. Legal suggestions (high level):

- Notice window: revise to 10 business days as the contractual default for scheduled penetration tests; allow a separate clause for an agreed accelerated window for pre-authorized vendors with a maximum of 72 hours.
- Scope: explicitly limit testing to non-production and scoped IP ranges; prohibit exfiltration or persistent admin backdoors.
- Evidence access: require read-only delivery of artifacts; access via pre-signed links or shared Drive only. No privileged console access unless agreed in writing.
- Data residency & redaction: allow Redwood to redact PII from operational artifacts; include a mechanism for Remedy to request unredacted artifacts under a tighter NDAs/inspection process.
- Acceptance: change wording from "will provide" to "will make available" for operational artifacts to clarify delivery vs custody.

I’ve attached a marked-up OrderForm_Redlines_20250709.docx with inline edits. From a legal perspective we should avoid one-off 48-hour defaults; better to keep a clear baseline (10 business days) and a documented escalation path for shorter notices.

If sales wants to move faster we can prepare a compact clause that allows Remedy to request one accelerated window per year with pre-agreed scope and insurance requirements.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_Redlines_20250709.docx (redline stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jul 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit language — negotiation approach

Team — thanks for the input. A few negotiation notes from sales:

- Remedy is a strategic mid-market account; getting them on a standard 7–10 day notice is fine, but we should offer the accelerated window option (one 48h or 72h per 12 months) as a commercial concession rather than a default term.
- Offer Remedy a SOC 2 snapshot (redacted) prior to signature to unblock procurement. This should be acceptable to legal with an NDA.
- If they push on evidence cadence, offer the first 30 days' weekly snapshots free as part of onboarding and then standard monthly cadence.

If legal can accept a 7–10 day baseline with a single negotiated accelerated test right, I’ll reopen the pricing discussion and push to signature.

- Ben
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@remedyhealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, procurement@remedyhealth.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2025 17:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions — pen test notice & evidence cadence

Hi Sarah — combining internal feedback and proposing a path forward to keep procurement moving. Recommendations below (summary + next steps):

Summary proposal (compromise):
- Standard pen-test notice: 7 business days (baseline).
- Accelerated window: Remedy may request one accelerated test window per 12-month period (up to 72 hours) for an agreed vendor and pre-approved scope. This is a commercial concession.
- Emergency tests: 72-hour notice for operational criticality only and require a joint pre-test call.
- Scope: strictly limited to non-production / staging systems and agreed IP ranges; no live production access or data exfiltration.
- Evidence cadence: weekly snapshots for the first 30 days (sample sets limited and redacted for PII), then monthly thereafter. Evidence delivery via secure Drive and expiring S3 links; access will be logged and we will provide an access report on request.
- SOC 2: we will provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) under NDA prior to signature.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached Draft_Security_Exhibit_v3.pdf and the redlined order form.
2) If Remedy agrees to the high-level proposal, I will send a DocuSign link for the Order Form and the Exhibit.
3) If Remedy wants an accelerated 48-hour default, we’ll need to escalate to my VP for a commercial exception — otherwise, the single accelerated window above is how we handle expedited requests.

DocuSign link for convenience: https://docusign.com/remedy-exhibit-sign
Secure evidence folder (example): https://drive.redwood.com/remedy-evidence

Thanks again — happy to hop on a short call if you prefer to walk through the exhibit and the sample evidence set.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
